mcp_tool_budget.mechanism: Hermes mcp_servers.<name>.tools.include (allowlist) / tools.exclude (blocklist), enforced at tool REGISTRATION (tools/mcp_tool.py, both the live-discovery and schema-cache paths), so a filtered tool's schema never reaches the model. fnmatch globs are supported. Claude/Codex/Grok/Kimi have no equivalent; there the whole server is the unit.

Full.why: No filter. Every tool registered. Use when authoring records in bulk and diagnosing in the same session.

Lean.why: Drops only the three tools whose parameter schemas carry full nested record objects: bulk_create (14,655 B), create_record (14,548 B) and bulk_apply (12,393 B) are 41,596 bytes between them -- a quarter of the server, and more than the whole of Skyrim Forge. They are dedicated bulk-authoring entry points, so a diagnosis or patch-reading session pays for them and never calls them. This is the shipped default because it costs no capability a normal session uses.

ReadOnly.why: Everything that reads, diagnoses, validates or looks up, and nothing that writes. Keeps load-order truth, conflict trees, cross-plugin queries, script/dialogue validation, the SKSE audit and the whole keyless Nexus surface. Drops the 18 write tools. Use for diagnosis, load-order work and Nexus research.

mcp_tool_budget.restore: hermes -p skyrim mcp configure housecarl  (interactive checklist, rewrites tools.include). Re-running the migrator will not undo a hand-edited filter.

components.name: codebase-memory-mcp
components.scope_note: Installed globally, enabled only through the project-scoped code-intel profile. NEVER enable --ui / install.ps1 --ui (Windows Codebase Discovery Open-With). auto_index=false auto_watch=false default.

components.note: Prefer npx codeburn (no large desktop bundle). Desktop Setup exe available on GitHub if desired.
components.name: CodeBurn
Impeccable
components.scope_note: The cross-provider skill is vendored from the official skill-v4.1.3 universal.zip and bound to its published SHA-256. The executable detector is the actually published npm 3.6.1 package, pinned by npm integrity. Optional Puppeteer is omitted: Playwright/browser profiles already own live rendering, and downloading a second browser would be duplication. Lifecycle scripts are disabled. UABS removes upstream self-update/pin paths and generated hook cache so provider skill trees keep one writer. Zero MCP schemas, daemon, account or key.

components.name: Skyrim Forge
components.note: Developed in this repository at BUNDLED-TOOLS/skyrim-forge; there is no separate SkyrimForge release. The installer resolves ONE versionless install root, migrates a version-stamped install onto it, preserves Workspaces and the virtualenv, wires selected providers, then proves the result runs with `forge doctor`.

components.name: Code Review Skill
components.scope_note: GENERIC languages only (C++, C#, PowerShell, Python, JS...). Skyrim-specific review stays with skyrim-code-review; Papyrus performance stays with papyrus-optimization.

components.name: Obsidian Skills (kepano)
components.scope_note: Markdown/vault/canvas authoring for _AI-SHARED-MEMORY and mod docs. Never used to author Skyrim records or framework INIs.

components.name: claude-mem
components.scope_note: CLAUDE CODE ONLY. Never install for Grok/Codex/Kimi/Hermes. Cross-session CONVERSATION memory (what was done, when, why) — does NOT replace codebase-memory-mcp (code structure graph) or skyrim-memory (verified Skyrim facts). Requires Bun on PATH (worker uses bun:sqlite). Worker port 37777. If red MCP errors: install Bun from https://bun.sh then restart Claude Code.
components.runtime_note: Bun required for worker daemon (https://bun.sh). The AIO installs Bun when missing, disables claude-mem's default anonymous telemetry, and starts the worker before reporting success.

components.name: Playwright MCP
components.scope_note: Browser automation for CLIs with no built-in browser. Claude Code already ships a browser pane, so it is skipped there. Never used for Nexus lookups - houseCARL does those keylessly. Measured 2026-09-02: 24 tools, 18,502 schema bytes, ~4,626 tokens per enabled turn. BROWSER CHOICE: with no flags, playwright-mcp defaults to the Google Chrome channel and prompts you to install Chrome. To use your own browser (Opera GX, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, ...), set user env PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH to the browser exe BEFORE running the installer - the wiring appends --executable-path automatically. Example (Opera GX): setx PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Opera GX\opera.exe". To change later, edit the args in your provider's MCP config (Grok/Codex config.toml, Kimi ~/.kimi-code/mcp.json). Pinned, not @latest: an unpinned npx server can change its tool surface mid-session, and npx will happily reuse a broken cache.

components.name: Firecrawl MCP
components.keyless_skip_reason: Keyless this server is 2 usable tools out of 25 (scrape, search) for 36,321 bytes of schema, ~9,080 tokens on EVERY turn - and those two duplicate the native web tools the providers already have. Not registered without a key; npx resolves this package on first launch, so nothing is cached either way and nothing is lost by waiting until the other 23 unlock. Override with -RegisterKeylessExtras.
components.keyless_note: Measured against the pinned 3.24.0 with FIRECRAWL_* scrubbed, all 25 tools called: exactly TWO work keyless - firecrawl_scrape and firecrawl_search. 21 answer 'Unauthorized: API key is required', including interact, which this note previously listed as keyless. firecrawl_extract is DEPRECATED ('deprecated and unavailable through MCP'), not key-gated. firecrawl_parse needs FIRECRAWL_API_URL pointing at a self-hosted instance, so Firecrawl's own docs saying 'Search, Scrape and Parse' are free do not hold for this server. Regenerate with TOOLS/measure_mcp_capability.py rather than editing by hand.
components.scope_note: Scraping general web docs (CommonLib docs, wikis, GitHub READMEs). NEVER Nexus Mods - houseCARL reads Nexus keylessly with changelogs and file lists.

components.name: Perplexity MCP
components.scope_note: REQUIRES PERPLEXITY_API_KEY (paid). Not installed on a keyless machine. Current-information research (new SKSE/CommonLib releases, game patch news). Never a substitute for houseCARL on Nexus, codebase-memory on code, or skyrim-memory on verified Skyrim facts.

components.name: Context7 Documentation MCP
components.keyless_note: Measured 2026-08-29 against the pinned 4.0.4 with the credential environment scrubbed: BOTH advertised tools answer keyless, nothing is rate-limited, key-gated or deprecated. `--api-key` / CONTEXT7_API_KEY is documented by the server's own --help and raises rate limits; it unlocks no additional tool. Regenerate with TOOLS/measure_mcp_capability.py rather than editing by hand.
components.scope_note: Current documentation for third-party libraries, frameworks, SDKs and CLIs, fetched per query instead of recalled from training data. Registered on every provider because it is the cheapest MCP server this pack ships: 2 tools, 4,870 bytes of schema, ~1,220 tokens per turn. Firecrawl by contrast costs 36,321 bytes for the same two usable keyless tools and is deliberately NOT registered without a key. Does not overlap codebase-memory: that indexes THIS repository's own symbols and call graph, context7 answers about code you did not write. No tool names collide.

components.name: GitHub MCP Server (official)
components.scope_note: GitHub's official server, replacing @modelcontextprotocol/server-github, which npm marks 'Package no longer supported'. Official release binaries since 1.5.0 carry GitHub's OAuth application: no PAT is required on github.com; the first authenticated tool call opens GitHub's browser authorization and keeps that token in the server process only. A GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN is optional and takes precedence when the user deliberately configures one. initialize + tools/list proves the binary and protocol, not completion of that later browser authorization. Registered with a scoped --toolsets list, not 'all': the server exposes 20 toolset groups and every enabled group costs tool-schema tokens on every turn. Widen it per project, never globally.

components.name: Serena
components.scope_note: Language-server-backed symbol search and editing. NOT registered globally and NOT registered machine-wide: TOOLS\Set-McpProfile.ps1 wires it for the one project that shows source-tree markers, because every connected server's tool schemas ride in context on every turn of every session that config covers. Claude Code takes it in projects["<abs path>"].mcpServers, Grok in the project's own .grok\config.toml; Codex, Kimi and Hermes have no project-scoped MCP config and are skipped unless -Global is passed. Registered with a per-client --context so the tool set is trimmed to what the client does not already provide -- Serena 1.7.0 ships one for claude-code, codex and grok, and Kimi/Hermes fall back to the generic 'agent' context -- and with --project <path> so it activates the project it was written for. Overlaps codebase-memory-mcp deliberately: that answers 'where is this in the graph', this answers 'what does this symbol resolve to, and rewrite its body'.

components.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
components.scope_note: Reads a live Chrome: console, network, performance traces, rendered DOM. The half playwright-mcp does not do -- playwright drives a browser, this explains what the browser did. Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing only; Chromium forks are not supported by this server, unlike playwright-mcp which takes PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH. --no-usage-statistics opts out of Google's telemetry, which is on by default upstream; this pack does not enable third-party telemetry on a user's machine without asking.

components.name: shadcn registry MCP
components.scope_note: Resolves registries from the project's components.json, so it is meaningless outside a shadcn project and is written project-scoped only. Measured 2026-09-02: 7 tools, 4,495 schema bytes, ~1,124 tokens per enabled turn.

components.name: Blender MCP
components.scope_note: Talks to an addon inside a running Blender. Pinned: `uvx blender-mcp` was version-free through 7.9.6, and an unpinned invocation can change its tool surface mid-session. `uvx blender-mcp@1.9.1 install-addon` places the addon, but ENABLING it is inside the editor and cannot be done from outside that process -- so the profile prints the step rather than claiming it ran it. Note the difference between 'the MCP executable starts' and 'the addon is connected': the server answers initialize with no Blender running at all, and only a tool call that reaches the scene proves the second. Blender is discovered from %APPDATA%\Blender Foundation, which Blender creates on first run whatever the install source -- 7.9.6 carried a maintainer's own Steam drive path here, which could never match on another machine. Measured 2026-09-02 with telemetry disabled and safe mode enabled: 1.9.1 answers initialize/tools-list with 28 tools and 29,274 schema bytes (~7,318 tokens per enabled turn). The profile writes BLENDER_MCP_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true and BLENDER_MCP_SAFE_MODE=true. Safe mode keeps normal bpy/bmesh/mathutils scene, render, save and import/export work while rejecting eval/exec/open, os/subprocess/network, persistence hooks and external .blend datablock loading before code reaches Blender.

components.name: Godot MCP
components.scope_note: Shells out to the Godot editor binary, which has no fixed install location on Windows, so the profile is gated on GODOT_PATH: setx GODOT_PATH "C:\path\to\Godot.exe".

components.name: Unity MCP
components.scope_note: There is no machine-wide Unity MCP server. The executable is generated inside the project's Library folder by the Unity package, so the entry is project-scoped by construction and its command is the resolved absolute path for that one project. Until the package is installed the exe does not exist, and the profile refuses rather than writing a path that is not there.

components.name: RTK (Rust Token Killer)
components.scope_note: CLI output filter with zero standing schema tokens. GIT CORPUS, measured on this repo AT rtk 0.47.0 against pinned refs: git diff v8.6.1..v8.6.5 430,285 -> 55,870 bytes (87%), git log v8.6.1..v8.6.5 14,250 -> 1,658 (88%), git diff v8.6.4..v8.6.5 33,453 -> 26,820 (20%), and git log --stat -20 v8.6.5 102,301 -> 102,301 (0%). Those are summaries, not lossless replacements: on the larger diff RTK retained 341 of 5,856 changed lines and omitted 5,515. Exact short status is different: a fixture covering staged, unstaged, deleted, renamed, Unicode and untracked paths was line-identical 5/5. NON-GIT CORPUS measured at 0.46.0 on 2026-08-27: rtk test kept the failure at about 93% saved; excluding truncating rows, the aggregate was 7.4% against git's 85.2%. TRUNCATION IS NOT SAVING: rtk json returned one of 5,425 array rows plus `... +5424 more`. rtk find works with a simple -name but breaks on compound predicates; rtk-ai/rtk#3410 reports its unconditional rewrite also intercepts find -delete/-exec. Archive correction: rtk test writes a complete tee for the measured 5.4 KB run and prints its path, but RTK documents a 1 MB raw tee cap. WINDOWS INTEGRATION, re-probed at 0.47.0 on 2026-09-02: upstream rewrite still catches lossy diff/log/show, broken find, cat/read, grep, curl, gh, and mutating git add/commit/push. Therefore broad upstream init and Hermes rtk-rewrite stay off. The bundle installs RTK by default and wires its own allowlist: exact standalone git status plus standalone human-facing pytest, cargo test and go test. Machine-readable output, pipes/redirection, all mutating Git, diff/show/log/find/search/read/curl/gh stay raw. Claude, Grok and Hermes receive the executable hook; Codex and Kimi receive the same narrow instruction because no trusted command-mutation hook is established there. Telemetry remains opt-in.

components.name: OMNI (context distillation)
components.scope_note: CLI + host hook, zero standing tokens -- same slot as rtk, different mechanism, so they stack rather than compete: rtk filters ONE command's output, OMNI remembers output across calls and returns a handle instead of resending what the agent already saw. USE THE README'S NUMBERS, NOT THE LANDING PAGE'S. The page headlines '97.2% off a file read twice' and '~24%'; the README's own corpus of 9,478 executions says '1.4% from the filters, 5.1% with the ledger'. 97.2% is a best case for one re-read, not an expected value -- treat 5% as the number and anything above it as a bonus. Ships a real x86_64-pc-windows-msvc binary with SHA256SUMS (v0.7.8, 2026-08-25), which is why it is here and lowfat is not: lowfat v0.8.0 publishes darwin and linux-gnu only and integrates through a POSIX shell eval hook, the same native-Windows degradation this catalog already documents for rtk's non-Hermes hooks. Full host rewrite on Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI; Hermes is supported; MCP-only fallback elsewhere. Stores a local SQLite ledger (permanent project knowledge, 30-day working data, 7-day verbatim traces) -- it is a cache of your own tool output, so treat it as project data, not a temp file. REWIND CAP, measured 2026-08-26 at 0.7.8: output above 65,536 bytes is truncated and NOT archived -- the marker says `full output not archived` and those bytes are unrecoverable, which the README's byte-for-byte guarantee does not qualify. Below the cap the guarantee holds and is self-verifying: the retrieve handle IS the content's SHA-256 prefix, and a 33,453-byte diff came back byte-identical. Head-to-head on this repo's git corpus: rtk 85.2%, OMNI 71.2% headline but only 6.4% once the truncated rows are excluded -- consistent with OMNI's own published 8.8% on git. Its value is the ledger, not the filter; see docs/TOOL-EVALUATIONS.md. Not auto-installed: a 5% saving does not justify rewriting every tool result on a machine by default.

components.name: Windows MCP
components.scope_note: Desktop control through UI Automation: click, type, send shortcuts, run PowerShell, read and write the registry and the filesystem, enumerate windows and processes. This is the one operating surface the pack had no way to reach -- Playwright and chrome-devtools stop at the browser. UIA also lets an agent PERCEIVE controls without spending a vision call, which is most of why it earns its schema. Measured 2026-08-27 with TOOLS\Measure-McpSchemaCost.ps1 against `uvx windows-mcp@0.8.5 serve`: 20 tools, 22,088 bytes, ~5,522 tokens on every turn while enabled -- less than firecrawl-mcp's 36,337 and about four times context7, for the whole desktop. OFF by default and never auto-detected: the `windows` profile carries no detect markers, so -Auto cannot reach it. Turn it on deliberately with TOOLS\Set-McpProfile.ps1 -Enable windows -Global. controls_machine is why TOOLS/measure_mcp_capability.py refuses to sweep it: that sweep calls every advertised tool with arguments synthesized from the schema, which here means typing into whatever window has focus and running whatever PowerShell the sample produces.

components.name: Super MCP Router
components.scope_note: A proxy MCP. It registers ONE server carrying 11 meta-tools and puts every other server behind on-demand discovery: search_tools by intent, get_tool_details for one schema, use_tool to call it. Measured 2026-08-27: 11 tools, 11,386 bytes, ~2,846 tokens per turn -- and that figure does NOT grow as more servers go behind it. The comparison that matters: houseCARL wired directly is 45 tools, 167,072 bytes, 41,768 tokens on EVERY turn, and Claude, Codex, Grok and Kimi cannot filter individual tools the way Hermes can, so on those four it is all 45 or nothing. Proven end to end against this pack's own houseCARL on 2026-08-27: search_tools('list the plugins in the active load order') -> get_tool_details (3,652 chars, ~913 tokens for that ONE schema) -> use_tool returned live data from the shim (2,999 mods, 2,995 plugins). Startup 1.2s, search 400ms, detail 200ms. NOT wired into a profile, and the reason is specific rather than cautious: the router reads its own config at %USERPROFILE%\.super-mcp\config.json, so enabling it means this pack writing and preserving a THIRD-PARTY tool's config file -- a second config writer with its own merge obligations, on a 24-star dependency. The measurement is what ships here; the wiring is its own release. One caveat to carry into that decision: BM25 ranking returned housecarl_merge_plugins FIRST for that read-only query, with the correct housecarl_load_order_status third. Discovery works, but the top hit is not automatically the safe one.

dotnet8-sdk.note: Needed to build/run Spooky from source

notes: Multi-provider Ultimate AI Starter Bundle. Includes optional full Skyrim SE/AE modding stack; not Skyrim-only.
spec_notes: MCP servers in this pack are local stdio; the 2026-07-28 stateless spec requires no change to them. Components carrying a 'profile' are NOT registered by the installer, and since 7.9.6 are not registered machine-wide either: BUNDLED-TOOLS/PROFILES.json holds their wiring and TOOLS/Set-McpProfile.ps1 applies a profile to ONE project -- the one whose markers asked for it -- when the machine satisfies its requirements. MCP tool schemas are in context on every turn, so a machine-wide registration is a permanent cost paid by every unrelated session; measured on a real machine, eight connected servers were 188 tool schemas per turn. Project scope means projects["<abs path>"].mcpServers in ~/.claude.json for Claude Code and <project>/.grok/config.toml for Grok; Codex, Kimi and Hermes have no project-scoped MCP config, so they are skipped with the reason printed rather than written machine-wide. Prove any registration with TOOLS/Test-McpHandshake.ps1.
